items.title: Section: The Summary Names All Nine Aspects, and the Treatise Explains — Heightened Mind Is the Ground of Shining Light

items.zh: 當知是名略說菩薩增上心住。謂心意樂作意思惟成滿趣入故；於一切行諸有情界及大菩提，能正通達故；於諸有情脫苦方便，能正推求故；於正法中起大恭敬，訪求無倦故；能正修行法隨法行，於其世俗諸靜慮等、等持、等至、無量神通，能引能住故；棄捨於彼，願自在力隨樂受生故；善根清淨故；受生故；神力故。若廣宣說，如十地經發光地說。由發聞行正法光明、等持光明之所顯示，是故此地名發光地。由內心淨能發光明，是故說名增上心住。由此義故，名發光地；即由此義，當知復名增上心住。
items.en:
Second, closing the brief meaning. One should understand this, in brief, as the bodhisattva's abode of heightened mind — namely, because purified-mind reflection brings entry to fulfilment; because formations, the realm of sentient beings, and great awakening are correctly penetrated; because the means for sentient beings' liberation from suffering is correctly sought out; because great reverence arises towards the true dharma, sought tirelessly; because dharma in accordance with dharma is correctly practised, able to bring forth and abide in mundane absorptions, concentrations, attainments, and immeasurable spiritual powers; because, relinquishing these, one takes rebirth as one wishes through the sovereign power of vow; because of purified wholesome roots; because of rebirth; because of majestic power.
Second, the broader pointer; first, pointing to the correspondence. Should one wish to hear it expounded at length, it is exactly as the Ten Grounds Sutra expounds it in its chapter on the ground of shining light. Because it is displayed through the light of hearing and practising the true dharma, and the light of meditative concentration, this ground is named the ground of shining light. Because inner purity of mind is able to give rise to light, this is why it is called the abode of heightened mind.
Second, explaining the name. Because of this meaning, it is named the ground of shining light; precisely because of this same meaning, one should understand it is also named the abode of heightened mind.

items.title: Section: The Abode Joined With the Factors of Awakening Opens — Ten Dharma-Lights of Entry, the Fourth Ground

items.zh: 云何菩薩覺分相應增上慧住？謂諸菩薩，先於增上心住，以求多聞增上力故，已得十法明入。由此十法明入成上品故，極圓滿故，超過增上心住，入初增上慧住。如是十法明入文詞，如契經說，應知其相。
items.en:
Fifth abode, joined with the factors of awakening; first, the question. What is a bodhisattva's abode joined with the factors of awakening?
Second, the answer; first, the brief account; first, distinguishing each mark; first, entry brought to fulfilment through the light of dharma; first, clarifying entry. Namely, bodhisattvas, previously at the abode of heightened mind, through the heightened power of seeking extensive learning, have already attained ten dharma-lights of entry. By these ten dharma-lights of entry becoming of the most excellent grade, utterly complete, one passes beyond the abode of heightened mind and enters the first abode of heightened wisdom.
Second, explaining the brief meaning. The wording of these ten dharma-lights of entry is exactly as the sutra explains; one should understand their mark accordingly.

items.title: Section: All Ten Dharma-Lights Detailed — From the Realm of Beings to the Great, Resolved Mind — Closing the First Aspect

items.zh: 謂若彼假設；若於中假設；若由此假設；若平等勝義；若染惱故、清淨故，成染成淨；若由繫縛煩惱所染；若由無上清淨所淨。當知是名十法明入略所說義。
items.en:
Commentary: Regarding "the wording of these ten dharma-lights of entry" and the like — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: if a bodhisattva, having attained the third bodhisattva ground and its complete, pure light, wishes to attain the fourth bodhisattva ground, should enter by ten dharma-lights, thereby attaining entry into the fourth ground. What are the ten? First, the light of entry contemplating the realm of sentient beings. Second, contemplating the realm of worlds. Third, contemplating the realm of dharmas. Fourth, contemplating the realm of space. Fifth, contemplating the realm of consciousness. Sixth, contemplating the desire realm. Seventh, contemplating the form realm. Eighth, contemplating the formless realm. Ninth, contemplating the realm of resolved faith in the superior mind. Tenth, contemplating the realm of resolved faith in the great mind. A bodhisattva, by these ten dharma-lights of entry, attains entry into the fourth ground.
Namely: that this-and-that is merely provisional designation; that within this there is likewise provisional designation; that by this very designation, other designations follow; that ultimate truth is everywhere equal; that, through affliction or through purity, defilement or purity results; that one is bound and defiled through affliction's own fetters; that one is purified through unsurpassed purity. One should understand this as the brief meaning of the ten dharma-lights of entry.

items.title: Section: Ten Kinds of Maturing Wisdom, Gathered Into Four — Growing Ever More Powerful Within the Tathāgata's Family

items.zh: 是諸菩薩住此住中，如契經說：不壞意樂而為上首，所有十種能成熟智、智成熟法皆悉成就。長如來家，得彼體法。
items.en:
Second aspect: attaining maturing wisdom and its dharma. Bodhisattvas abiding in this abode, exactly as the sutra explains, take unwavering aspiration as foremost, and all ten kinds of maturing wisdom and the dharma matured thereby are fully accomplished. Growing established within the Tathāgata's own family, one attains that very substance.
Commentary: Regarding "unwavering aspiration as foremost" and the like — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: by ten kinds of dharma-wisdom, teaching and maturing beings. First, an unwavering mind. Second, decisive, ultimate reverence towards the three jewels. Third, discerning observation of arising and ceasing formations. Fourth, discerning observation that dharmas are, by their own nature, unarisen. Fifth, discerning observation of the world's formation and destruction. Sixth, discerning observation that karmic action gives rise to birth. Seventh, discerning observation of the world and of nirvana. Eighth, discerning observation of the distinct karma of different worlds of sentient beings. Ninth, discerning observation of the distinction between the prior and later boundary. Tenth, discerning observation that everything has nothing whatsoever that could be exhausted. O sons of the buddhas! A bodhisattva, by these ten kinds of dharma-wisdom teaching and maturing beings, thereby grows in power within the Tathāgata's own family, attaining that inner dharma itself.

items.title: Section: Cultivating the Thirty-Seven Factors of Awakening, the Four Foundations of Mindfulness Foremost

items.zh: 觀一切種菩提薩埵增上力故，修四念住而為上首三十七種菩提分法。
items.en:
Third aspect: cultivating the factors of awakening. Observing every kind of heightened power belonging to awakening and to sentient beings, one cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness as foremost among the thirty-seven kinds of factors of awakening.
Commentary: Regarding "observing every kind of heightened power belonging to awakening and sentient beings" — this means that observing every kind of awakening together with sentient beings themselves is able to cause the practice remedying affliction to increase; this is called heightened power. As the sutra says, observing the wisdom of every kind of wisdom, never abandoning the mind set on every sentient being.

items.title: Section: The Most Subtle, Innate View of Self Finally Severed — Root of Every Other View and of Pride Itself

items.zh: 如契經說：由於此法方便攝受勤修習故，最極微細薩迦耶見，執著一切蘊、界、處等一切動亂，皆得畢竟不現行斷。
items.en:
Fourth aspect: severing subtle views, attachment, and disturbance. As the sutra explains: through the skilful means gathered in this dharma, diligently cultivated, the most extremely subtle view of a substantial self, the attachment grasping at the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields, and every disturbance this generates, are now entirely severed from manifesting again.
Commentary: Regarding "the most extremely subtle view of a substantial self" and the like — this view of a substantial self is born together with the body itself, and this is why it is called most extremely subtle. This is the root, able to give rise to every other wrong view and to self-conceit as well; this is called the attachment grasping at the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields, and every disturbance this generates. All of this is entirely extinguished; this is called permanently ended from manifesting again. One should understand this is exactly the fruit of increased diligence in remedying affliction.

items.title: Section: Restrained Conduct Ended, Praised Conduct Followed — The Fruit of Increased Karmic Remedy

items.zh: 由彼斷故，一切如來所呵毀業皆不現行，一切如來所讚美業如實隨轉。
items.en:
Fifth aspect: restrained and permitted conduct, dwelling apart from over-familiarity. Because that view is severed, every conduct the Tathāgatas condemn no longer manifests at all, and every conduct the Tathāgatas praise is genuinely, correctly followed.
Commentary: Regarding "every conduct the Tathāgatas condemn" and the like — this displays the fruit of increased remedy against karmic action itself. Whatever action is tainted by affliction should not be done — this is exactly what the Tathāgatas condemn. Whatever accords with bodhisattva conduct should be done — this is exactly what the Tathāgatas praise.

items.title: Section: The Mind Grows Supple, Gentle, and Purified — Nine Kinds of Nourished Mind From the Ten Grounds Sutra

items.zh: 既如是已，其心轉復滋潤、柔和，有所堪能；其心轉復種種行相皆善清淨。
items.en:
Sixth aspect: the mind grows supple and thoroughly purified. Having accomplished this, such a bodhisattva's mind grows nourished and gentle, genuinely capable; every kind of its own activity becomes wholesome and pure.
Commentary: Regarding "the mind grows nourished and gentle" and the like — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: in this way, one accomplishes a nourished mind, a soft mind, a tamed mind, a mind of peaceful ease, an undefiled mind, a mind ever seeking superior and higher conduct, a mind ever seeking superior wisdom, a mind that rescues the entire world, a mind reverent towards every teacher and compliant in receiving instruction, and a mind that practices in accordance with whatever dharma is heard. What is said here as "nourished" is exactly that nourished mind. What is said as "gentle" is exactly the soft mind. What is said as "genuinely capable" is exactly the tamed mind. What is said as "every kind of activity wholesome and pure" is exactly the mind of peaceful ease through the mind practising in accordance with what is heard. Since all these minds are displayed through remedying faults, this is why it is said in total as "every kind of activity."

items.title: Section: Knowing Kindness and Repaying It — Nine Forms of Gratitude, From Reverence to Never Misconstruing the Teacher's Own Meaning

items.zh: 又善知恩、知報恩等隨順意樂，種種白法、皆悉成就。
items.en:
Seventh aspect: aspiration accords, wholesome qualities abound. Furthermore, skilfully knowing kindness received, skilfully knowing how to repay it, and every aspiration according with this — every kind of wholesome dharma is thereby accomplished.
Commentary: Regarding "skilfully knowing kindness" and the like — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: this bodhisattva thus accomplishes a mind that knows kindness, a mind that repays it, growing gentle, dwelling together in peace; a straightforward mind, a gentle mind; a mind free of any dense thicket of conduct, free of flattery or crookedness, free of pride; skilfully receiving instruction, grasping the speaker's own meaning. In this way a wholesome mind is accomplished, a quiescent mind is accomplished, a wholesome, quiescent mind is accomplished. This should be explained exactly as there. That wholesome mind, quiescent mind, and wholesome quiescent mind are exactly this text's own "every kind of wholesome dharma," one should understand.

items.title: Section: Great, Unflagging Diligence — the Lute String Neither Too Taut Nor Too Slack

items.zh: 尋求上地能修治業，發大精進，逮得安住。
items.en: Eighth aspect: seeking higher undertakings, arousing great diligence. Seeking out the higher ground and the practice able to remedy karmic action there, one arouses great diligence, thereby attaining genuine, abiding stability.

items.title: Section: Purified Aspiration Becomes Settled Disposition — Cross-Referencing the Seven Aspects of Compassion Back in Fascicle 47

items.zh: 由此因緣，所有意樂、增上意樂勝解界性，皆得圓滿。
items.en:
Ninth aspect: cultivating pure aspiration into a resolute-understanding causal nature. By these causes and conditions, every kind of aspiration, heightened aspiration, and resolute-understanding causal nature is brought to complete fulfilment.
Commentary: Regarding "every kind of aspiration, heightened aspiration" and the like — the chapter on excellent aspiration says: a bodhisattva, towards sentient beings, deeply arouses seven aspects of compassion, called excellent aspiration and utterly excellent aspiration (fascicle 47, page 3760 of the Nanjing edition). This is exactly this text's own "aspiration." It further says: one should understand that here, pure faith taking the lead, discerning choice of dharma taking the lead, resolute understanding and settled confidence regarding the buddha-dharmas, this is called a bodhisattva's own heightened aspiration (fascicle 47, page 3763 of the Nanjing edition). Such aspiration and heightened aspiration, through the power of resolute understanding, become a habituated, settled disposition — this is called resolute-understanding causal nature. This is brought to fulfilment through the great diligence already described as its own cause and condition.

items.title: Section: Demonic Forces and Rival Teachings Unable to Shake This Resolve

items.zh: 由是因緣，一切外道、種種魔軍、聖教怨敵，不能映奪、不能傾動。
items.en:
Tenth aspect: demonic and hostile forces unable to shake this resolve. By these causes and conditions, every non-Buddhist path, every kind of demonic force, and every hostile power opposed to the noble teaching are entirely unable to obscure or overturn it, entirely unable to shake it.
Commentary: Regarding "every non-Buddhist path, every kind of demonic force" and the like — this follows from the previous fulfilment of resolute-understanding causal nature as its own cause and condition; this is why all such forces are entirely unable to obscure, overturn, or shake it.

items.title: Section: Gold Wrought Into an Ornament, and Wisdom Blazing Like a Jewel No Storm Can Extinguish

items.zh: 廣見諸佛、善根清淨，廣說如前，應知其相。此差別者，謂如世間善巧工匠，以所鍊金作莊嚴具，非餘未作莊嚴具金之所映奪。如是此中菩薩善根，非餘安住凡住菩薩所有善根所能映奪。如末尼寶所放光明，非餘寶珠所能映奪，一切世間風水雨等，不能斷滅所放光明。如是此中菩薩所有智慧光明，一切聲聞及獨覺等不能映奪，一切魔怨不能斷滅。
items.en:
Eleventh aspect: purified wholesome roots; first, the general account; first, pointing to what was already said. Broadly beholding the buddhas, wholesome roots purified, explained at length exactly as before; one should understand their mark accordingly.
Second, a simile marking the difference. The difference is this: just as, in the world, a skilful craftsman's own smelted gold, wrought into an ornament, cannot be outshone by gold not yet so wrought — so too this bodhisattva's own wholesome roots cannot be outshone by any bodhisattva still abiding at an ordinary, unenlightened stage.
Second, a further simile specifically for the faculty of wisdom. Just as light radiating from a wish-fulfilling jewel cannot be outshone by any other jewel, and every worldly wind, water, and rain cannot extinguish the light it radiates — so too this bodhisattva's own wisdom-light cannot be outshone by any hearer or solitary-realiser, and no demonic, hostile force whatsoever can extinguish it.

items.title: Section: Rebirth as the Lord of the Suyāma Heaven, Teaching Beings to Uproot the View of Self

items.zh: 受生多作蘇夜摩天王，善化有情，令其除滅薩迦耶見。
items.en: Twelfth aspect: rebirth. Taking rebirth, one most often becomes the lord of the Suyāma heaven, skilfully transforming sentient beings, causing them to eliminate the view of a substantial self.

items.title: Section: Majestic Power Now Reaching a Koṭi of Each Kind — Closing the Thirteenth and Final Aspect

items.zh: 所有威力，於前住中說百千數，當知此中說俱胝數。
items.en: Thirteenth aspect: majestic power. Whatever majestic power was already described in the previous abode as a hundred thousand of each kind, one should understand that here it is described as a koṭi of each kind.

items.title: Section: The Summary Names All Thirteen Aspects, and the Treatise Confirms — This Is the Ground of Blazing Wisdom

items.zh: 當知是名略說菩薩覺分相應增上慧住。謂法明入成滿得入故；成就智故；修習菩提分法故；薩迦耶見等一切執著動亂斷故；制業、開業遠離習近故；由是因緣心調柔故；隨順功德皆隆盛故；依所尋求修治地業發大精進故；由是因緣，所有意樂、增上意樂勝解界性淨修治故；由是因緣，一切聖教所有怨敵不能映奪及傾動故；善根清淨故；受生故；威力故。若廣宣說，如十地經焰慧地說。於此地中，菩提分法如實智焰，能成正法教慧照明，是故此地名焰慧地。又即彼地，此中說名覺分相應增上慧住。
items.en:
Second, closing the brief meaning. One should understand this, in brief, as the bodhisattva's abode joined with the factors of awakening — namely, because entry is brought to fulfilment through the light of dharma; because of maturing wisdom; because the factors of awakening are cultivated; because the view of a substantial self and every attachment and disturbance it generates are severed; because of restrained and permitted conduct, dwelling apart from over-familiarity; because, through these causes, the mind grows supple; because wholesome qualities, according with this, all abound; because, seeking out the practice remedying the higher ground, great diligence is aroused; because, through these causes, aspiration, heightened aspiration, and resolute-understanding causal nature are purified and cultivated; because, through these causes, every hostile power opposed to the noble teaching is unable to obscure or shake it; because of purified wholesome roots; because of rebirth; because of majestic power.
Second, the broader pointer; first, pointing to it. Should one wish to hear it expounded at length, it is exactly as the Ten Grounds Sutra expounds it in its chapter on the ground of blazing wisdom.
Second, explaining. Within this ground, the blazing flame of genuine wisdom regarding the factors of awakening is able to accomplish teaching the true dharma with an illuminating wisdom; this is why this ground is named the ground of blazing wisdom.
Third, the correspondence. This very same ground is exactly what is here called the abode joined with the factors of awakening.

blocks.text: The fourth ground cultivates the thirty-seven factors of awakening, and here the subtlest view of self finally stops arising.

"Displaying the light of hearing and practising the Dharma, and the light of equipoise: hence the Radiant Ground." Venerable Miào Jìng: the light of hearing is wisdom from hearing; the light of equipoise is wisdom from cultivation.

Master Cháng Bǎi: entering more deeply into the Tathāgata's teaching is "dharma-light entry". Venerable Miào Jìng: "sentient being" is a provisional term for the five aggregates combined. Master Cháng Bǎi: names like John and Jane are provisional distinctions.
Venerable Miào Jìng: the wholesome roots are what is matured; wisdom is what matures them.
"Cultivating the four foundations of mindfulness as foremost among the thirty-seven factors." Master Cháng Bǎi: without beings a bodhisattva cannot become a buddha.

Master Cháng Bǎi: coarse self-view comes from conceptual discrimination; the subtlest is innate. Here only its manifestation stops; the seed is cut only at the vajra-like concentration. Venerable Miào Jìng: self-view is the root of every clinging.
Master Cháng Bǎi: restrained conduct is what the Buddha forbids; meditation and recitation retreats are conduct the Tathāgata praises.
Venerable Miào Jìng: a rigid pulse means illness, a supple pulse health. Without the nourishment of calm and insight, the mind is rigid.
Master Cháng Bǎi: knowing kindness and repaying it are two acts; not giving rise to greed, hatred, and delusion repays the Buddha.
Master Cháng Bǎi: fourth-ground bodhisattvas have unceasing diligence, yet they do not go without sleep; a string too taut sounds bad and snaps easily.

"Refined gold wrought into an ornament cannot be outshone by gold not yet wrought." Master Cháng Bǎi: below the fourth ground they only refine the gold; the fourth makes it into necklaces and bracelets.
The lute string comes from the Buddha's advice to the monk Soṇa, who practised so hard his feet bled. Even on the fourth ground, diligence includes sleep.

quiz.q: Why is the abode of heightened mind called the "Radiant Ground"? How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish the two lights?
options: the light of hearing is wisdom from hearing; the light of equipoise is wisdom from cultivation
quiz.why: "Displaying the light of hearing and practising the dharma, and the light of equipoise — hence the Radiant Ground." Venerable Miào Jìng: the light of hearing is wisdom from hearing; the light of equipoise is wisdom from cultivation.

quiz.q: To enter the abode joined with the factors of awakening, what had the bodhisattva attained at the previous abode?
options: through seeking extensive learning, ten dharma-lights of entry
quiz.why: "Through seeking extensive learning, ten dharma-lights of entry had already been attained." Master Cháng Bǎi: entering more deeply into the Tathāgata's teaching is "dharma-light entry."

quiz.q: In the brief meaning, "what is provisionally designated" — how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "sentient being"?
options: "being" is a provisional designation — the five aggregates combined, named "being"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "sentient being" is a provisional term — form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness combined, provisionally named. Master Cháng Bǎi: names like John and Jane are provisional distinctions.

quiz.q: In "ten kinds of maturing wisdom and dharma matured thereby," how does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish the maturing and the matured?
options: wholesome roots are what is matured; wisdom is what matures
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the wholesome roots are what is matured; wisdom is what matures. Master Cháng Bǎi: from the first to the tenth ground, faith in the Mahāyāna never regresses.

quiz.q: In cultivating the factors of awakening, what does the fourth-ground bodhisattva take as foremost?
options: the four foundations of mindfulness, foremost among the thirty-seven
quiz.why: "Cultivating the four foundations of mindfulness as foremost among the thirty-seven factors." Master Cháng Bǎi: without beings a bodhisattva cannot become a buddha — great wisdom and great compassion.

quiz.q: At the fourth ground, "the most subtle view of self" is severed. What do the lectures say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: coarse self-view is conceptual, the subtlest innate; here its manifestation is cut, the seed only at vajra-like concentration; Miào Jìng: self-view is the root of all clinging
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: coarse self-view arises from conceptual discrimination, the subtlest is innate; here only its manifestation stops — the seed is cut only at vajra-like concentration. Venerable Miào Jìng: self-view is the root of every clinging.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "restrained" and "permitted" conduct?
options: restrained conduct is what the Buddha forbids, permitted conduct the good he allows — meditation and recitation retreats are praised conduct
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: restrained conduct is what the Buddha forbids; permitted conduct is the good he allows; meditation and recitation retreats are conduct the Tathāgata praises.

quiz.q: "The mind grows nourished and gentle, capable." What image does Venerable Miào Jìng use?
options: a rigid pulse means illness, a supple pulse health — a supple mind is practice
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: a rigid pulse means illness, a supple pulse health; a supple mind is practice; without the nourishment of calm and insight, the mind is rigid.

quiz.q: "Seeking higher grounds, arousing great diligence." What image does Master Cháng Bǎi use?
options: a string too taut sounds bad and snaps — fourth-ground diligence is unceasing but not sleepless
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: fourth-ground bodhisattvas have unceasing diligence, yet don't go without sleep; a string too taut sounds bad and snaps easily. Venerable Miào Jìng: not yet a buddha, they seek higher accomplishment.

quiz.q: "Skilfully knowing and repaying kindness" — how does Master Cháng Bǎi describe repaying the Buddha?
options: not giving rise to greed, hatred, delusion is repaying the Buddha
quiz.why: "Skilfully knowing and repaying kindness, and every aspiration according with this." Master Cháng Bǎi: knowing kindness and repaying it are two acts; not arising greed, hatred, and delusion repays the Buddha.

quiz.q: In the fourth ground's simile, what is the gold made into, and why can it not be outshone?
options: wrought into an ornament, not outshone by unwrought gold
quiz.why: "Refined gold wrought into an ornament cannot be outshone by gold not yet wrought." Master Cháng Bǎi: below the fourth ground they only refine the gold; the fourth makes it into necklaces and bracelets.
